info.title: ATB API
info.description:
The Automated Topology Builder API, version 1.

Authenticate with an API key sent as `Authorization: Bearer atb_...`. Errors are
RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`) whose `type` ends in a stable
slug. Every keyed response carries `RateLimit-*` and `X-ATB-Daily-*` headers.
The Python client is the `atb-client` package.

get.description:
Search the molecules this key can see, in molid order.

With no filter at all this walks every visible molecule. `total` is present only
when the whole result fits on this page (the first page, with no `next_cursor`):
a `COUNT(*)` over a visibility-filtered, LIKE-filtered join is exactly the cost the
cursor exists to avoid.

get.description:
Visible molecules whose row changed since the cursor, oldest change first.

"Changed" is any of the timestamps the pipeline stamps on the row moving: submission,
a claim (`start_time`), finishing (`finish_time`) or a topology build recorded in
`atb_py_revdate`. A topology regenerated in the cache *without* moving
`atb_py_revdate` -- which happens -- is not visible here; the `topology.regenerated`
event (WP3/WP6) is what will carry that. Costs no quota, but it is a scan of
`molecules` (no index covers these columns): ~0.8 s on production.

parameters.name: since

schema.description: A `next_cursor` from a previous call, or an RFC 3339 time. Default: the last 24 hours.
schema.title: Since

parameters.description: A `next_cursor` from a previous call, or an RFC 3339 time. Default: the last 24 hours.

get.description:
A molecule's metadata, its status and its current topology hash, with a strong
`ETag`. `If-None-Match` with the current tag answers `304` and costs nothing.

301.description: A merged duplicate: `Location` names the canonical molecule.

get.description: Plan D9's status resource. Free: this is what `wait()` polls.

Every stored topology version, per force field, newest first. A version is
servable while its directory exists; none of them can be regenerated once gone.

Which QM result each level's topology was built from. The record itself --
coordinates, charges, the Hessian -- is the restricted `qm_data` file.

The vacuum energy-minimisation check (`emin_vac`): the RMSD in nm between the
QM geometry and the minimised one, or why there is none. `emin_vac.vacuum_rmsd_status`
decides, exactly as the molecule page does.

TI solvation free energies and the experimental values for the same compound.

The molecule page's query (`site_pages/molecule.py`, `TI_panels`), with the
TI -> experimental solvent mapping of `TI_plots.EXPERIMENTAL_SOLVENTS_FOR_TI_SOLVENT`
applied in Python rather than as a SQL CASE. As on the page, only an ordinary
(curation_trust 0) molecule reports TI results. Every result is returned; `current`
marks the newest per solvent and method, which is the one the site plots.

The bonded-assignment record of a stored topology: which library motif, at
which rung, gave each bond, angle and torsion its parameters, plus the angle-sum
reconciliation. Read from the served topology's own `yml_moldata`, as the molecule
page's panel does (`helpers/bonded_parameters.read_blocks`), never re-derived.

The molecule's tautomer/protomer family (the visible members) and each member's
lowest QM energy per qm_type. The family is the `compound_graph_keys` skeleton-key
group where that table exists, else the legacy stereo-blind `tautomer_group_id`
(`helpers/graph_keys` decides, as the molecule page does). Members are filtered as
the page's tautomer table filters them (curation_trust 0, qm_level >= 1), so the
molecule itself may be absent from its own family. A skeleton-key family is every
form of one heavy-atom skeleton -- tautomers, protomers, stereoisomers and other
hydrogenation states alike -- so group members by `formula` and `netcharge` to
compare energies. A molecule in no group is reported alone.

Other molecules of the same compound -- alternative conformations of one
structure -- with their wB97X/6-31G(d) SMD-water energies, as v0.1's
`molecules/conformations` reports them. Visible molecules only.

One deliberate difference: v0.1 filters `qm_type = ... OR qm_type IS NULL` in the
WHERE clause, which drops a molecule whose only energies are of another qm_type;
here the qm_type is part of the join, so such a molecule is listed with no energy.

Every file of the vocabulary for one topology version and force field, with
whether it exists now. Restricted files are listed only to keys that may read them.
v0.1-only names are listed when the file exists.

get.description:
One file, streamed. `name` is a v1 name or any v0.1 name.

TEMPORARY (WP2): a topology file that is not cached is a `409
generation-required` problem -- this route never generates. WP3 makes a miss a
job under the `?wait=` convention.

301.description: A merged duplicate: `Location` names the canonical molecule.

409.description: generation-required: not cached; WP3 will generate it as a job.

410.description: topology-version-gone: the requested hash is no longer stored.

post.description:
Pairwise RMSDs between 2 to 10 structures (PDB texts and/or molids), each pair
optimally aligned by `Blind_RMSD` as v0.1's `rmsd/matrix` does. `rmsd` is the
two-structure answer. Molids must be visible to the key; a merged duplicate is
compared as its canonical molecule. Weight 2: the work is O(n²) alignments.
